title: Mental Well-being Circles Formed under SG Mental Well-being Network
what_it_is: Mental Well-being Circles Formed under SG Mental Well-being Network

sections.label: Mental Well-Being Circles progress
sections.summary: The Network has six Mental Well-Being Circles with 400 trained volunteers and around 30 partners, still trying different approaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Network has set up six Mental Well-Being Circles across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: There are now 400 trained volunteers and around 30 partners, across the six Mental Well-Being Circles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: The Well-Being Circles are still relatively new and are trying different approaches and models.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
sentences.text: While it would be too soon to be definitive about the learning points, I assure the Member that we will gain valuable experience over time and apply the lessons that we have learnt.

sections.label: Purpose of Mental Well-Being Circles
sections.summary: The Circles aim to raise mental well-being awareness, train peer supporters, and provide a network for mutual support and referrals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The purpose of the Mental Well-Being Circles was born out of the Youth Mental Well-Being Network and expanded to the SG Mental Well-Being Network – the purpose is to raise awareness about mental well-being and mental health issues; and also to train peer supporters so that they may be able to support their friends, their families and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And thirdly, it is to have a network for them to support one another and, if necessary, to refer people who need step-up care to step-up support.
